rationale: The blind reconstruction and pinned Theorem 2.6.3 state the same weighted general Hoeffding inequality. Both quantify one universal positive absolute constant over all finite nonempty independent centered sub-gaussian real families, all deterministic real coefficient vectors, and all t >= 0. Both use the two-sided absolute-value event, prefactor 2, and rate c t^2/(K^2 ||a||_2^2), with K the maximum psi_2 norm. The translation's explicit probability-space machinery, integrability, arbitrary finite index type, infimum construction of psi_2, and totalized zero-denominator semantics are faithful expansions or harmless boundary handling, not substantive extra hypotheses or missing cases.
